extracted.intended_audience: poets, creative-writing students, literary critics, and philosophers interested in imagination, memory, and the theory of association
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and theoretical criteria about the imagination, memory, and laws of association as they bear on poetic composition and recollection. Emphasizes the active/passive nature of imagination, what determines recall, and practical 'arts of memory' for creative work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Imagination as an intermediate faculty (active and passive)
rubrics_metrics.description: There are two powers at work, which relatively to each other are active and passive; this implies an intermediate faculty which is at once both active and passive — in philosophical language, the Imagination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the imagination as a faculty that both receives impressions (passive) and exerts control (active). The account argues that this reciprocal activity is necessary for voluntary thought, perception, and for composing; references Schelling and Maasz for definitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poetic imagination requires superior degree plus voluntary control
rubrics_metrics.description: In common language, and especially on the subject of poetry, the name 'imagination' is appropriated to a superior degree of the faculty, joined to a superior voluntary control over it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For poetry, cultivate not merely vivid fancy but intentional control over imaginative processes — i.e., training to direct, intensify, and shape imaginative contents when composing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contemporaneity (continuity) is a condition of association but not its full cause
rubrics_metrics.description: Contemporaneity (Leibnitz's law of continuity) is the common condition of all the laws of association and a component element in the material subjects; yet contemporaneity is the limit/condition of association, distinct from the particular cause of recall.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When analyzing how images or ideas associate in composition, distinguish the general condition (things co-existing in time/space) from the specific cause that makes one part of an impression recalled in preference to others.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vividness (intensity/distinctness) determines recall within a total impression
rubrics_metrics.description: Whatever makes certain parts of a total impression more vivid or distinct than the rest will determine the mind to recall these in preference to others equally linked together by contemporaneity (continuity).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To prompt desired recollection while composing, increase the vividness or distinctness of target elements (through emphasis, repetition, contrast, etc.). Examples: seeing a mackerel recalling gooseberries because they co-existed as sauce; likeness and contrast produce further recalls (goose → swan).

rubrics_metrics.name: The will can arbitrarily give vividness by intensifying attention
rubrics_metrics.description: The will itself, by confining and intensifying the attention, may arbitrarily give vividness or distinctness to any object whatsoever.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Active, volitional attention is a technique to enhance memory and control associative recall — implying training focused attention is more effective than mechanical mnemonic tricks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arts of Memory: sound logic, knowledge, temper, conscience, health
rubrics_metrics.description: Sound logic; philosophical knowledge of facts under cause and effect; a cheerful and communicative temper disposing us to notice similarities and contrasts; a quiet conscience; a condition free from anxieties; sound health; and above all (for passive remembrance) a healthy digestion — these are the best, the only Arts of Memory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical regimen for sustaining memory and creative faculty: cultivate logical habits, factual/philosophical understanding, sociable cheerfulness, moral quietude, avoid anxiety, maintain physical health and good digestion. These natural habits are preferable to artificial mnemonic schemes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reject artificial memory schemes that debase the fancy
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain recent schemes which promise an artificial memory can only produce a confusion and debasement of the fancy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid mechanical mnemonic systems that aim to force memory by trickery; they risk corrupting imaginative powers and producing disorder in associative thought. Favor practices that enhance natural vividness and voluntary attention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish conditions from causes and essence (avoid sophism)
rubrics_metrics.description: The paralogisms that permit mechanical theories arise from mistaking the conditions of a thing for its causes and essence, and the process by which we arrive at the knowledge of a faculty for the faculty itself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In theorizing about creative faculties, do not conflate external regularities (conditions of perceiving/learning) with the mental powers themselves. For writers: be careful attributing creative effects to surface conditions without recognizing underlying faculties (e.g., confusing 'seeing' with 'having eyes').

rubrics_metrics.name: Composition alternates active resistance and passive yielding
rubrics_metrics.description: The process of composing is analogous to a little water-insect winning its way up a stream by alternate pulses of active and passive motion, now resisting the current, and now yielding to it in order to gather strength.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize composition as an alternation between deliberate, effortful control and receptive, yielding phases where unconscious or associative material can accumulate and then be used; cultivate both modes rather than forcing continuous effort.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain the reality of will and reason against reductive associationism
rubrics_metrics.description: If will, reason, judgment and understanding are represented as mere products of blind mechanical association, the soul becomes a 'mere ens logicum' and creative agency is undermined; such reduction has deep moral and theological consequences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As a working principle for creative authorship, preserve a conception of the self as an active agent — accountable, intentional, and capable of directing associations — rather than accepting a view that reduces creativity to passive mechanical effects.
